title: Context management
summary: Keeps the always-loaded context small and the prompt cache stable: instruction-file cap, procedure delivery, noisy-work placement, cache hygiene, compaction timing and watcher noise.

questions.prompt: How many lines may the always-loaded instruction file (AGENTS.md) have?

options.label: 150 lines
options.tradeoff: Cheapest on every request and subagent; forces detail into skills.

options.label: 300 lines
options.tradeoff: More inline guidance; roughly double the steady token cost.

options.label: No cap
options.tradeoff: No friction; the file grows and every request pays for it.

questions.prompt: How are detailed procedures delivered to the agent?

options.label: Skills loaded on demand
options.tradeoff: Procedure text costs tokens only when used; relies on skill descriptions triggering.

options.label: Always-on rules
options.tradeoff: Reliably present; paid on every request.

options.label: One-line pointers to docs
options.tradeoff: Smallest footprint; the agent must choose to read the doc.

questions.prompt: Where does noisy work (search, logs, test output) run?

options.label: Delegate to a subagent only when the cost model says the handoff is cheaper
options.tradeoff: Keeps the main context lean without paying handoff costs that do not pay off.

options.label: Always delegate to a subagent
options.tradeoff: Cleanest main context; pays a handoff and cold cache on every delegation.

options.label: Run inline
options.tradeoff: No handoff cost; noise stays in context and is re-read on every request.

questions.prompt: How is the prompt cache protected from mid-task model, effort or instruction-file changes?

options.label: Advisory instruction plus a confirm-before-switch hook where the host has one
options.tradeoff: Strongest protection available; a confirmation prompt on legitimate switches.

options.label: Advisory instruction only
options.tradeoff: No prompts; nothing stops an accidental cache-busting change.

options.label: None
options.tradeoff: No friction; each switch can re-pay a cold cache.

options.label: At task boundaries
options.tradeoff: Keeps the cache warm mid-task and drops finished work; needs discipline at each boundary.

options.label: When the host decides
options.tradeoff: No effort; may compact mid-task and lose detail or cache.

options.label: Fresh session per task
options.tradeoff: Cleanest context; pays the cold start every task.

questions.prompt: How many notifications may a watcher (a script that syncs on a CI run, a long command or a log) send?

options.label: Quiet: state changes and a summary, at most 6 an hour
options.tradeoff: Fewest woken turns; can hide a line you wanted.

options.label: Normal: changes, at most 30 an hour
options.tradeoff: More detail; each notification can wake a turn that re-reads the context.

options.label: Verbose: every line except repeats
options.tradeoff: Nothing hidden; a busy watch wakes many turns.

decisions.title: The always-loaded instruction file is capped at 150 lines
decisions.body:
## Decision

Keep `AGENTS.md`, the always-loaded instruction file, at or under 150 lines (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}). Host instruction files that are symlinks to it share the cap.

## Why

Every always-loaded token is paid on every request and every subagent; cached prefixes stay cheap only if stable (facts 0003, 0011).

guardrails.title: The instruction file must stay within 150 lines

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the cap decision, every line past it is paid on every request.

enforcement.check: AGENTS.md line count within the cap

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Keep `AGENTS.md` within 150 lines; move detail into skills.

decisions.title: Watchers are quiet
decisions.body:
## Decision

Watchers started through `go-getter watch` report state changes and a final summary, collapse duplicates and bursts (60 s window) and stop after 6 notifications an hour with one notice; `--until done` prints one result. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}.)

## Why

Each watcher line can wake a model turn that re-reads the whole context from cache, and hosts offer no throttle.

guardrails.title: Watches start through go-getter watch, --until done for CI runs and long commands

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the noise decision, a watch started outside the wrapper is not throttled.

enforcement.check: Where no hook wraps the watch, start it through `go-getter watch`
Pre-tool hook wraps the host watcher command in `go-getter watch` where the host allows

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Start watches through `go-getter watch`; use `--until done` for CI runs and long commands. Where the host allows, the pre-tool hook wraps the watch command.
